newsitem.title: INDIA: British zoos ask India to send elephant trainers.
newsitem.headline: British zoos ask India to send elephant trainers.

text.p: The British Federation of Zoos has asked India for 10 elephant-keepers to help with training elephants and their British keepers, an Indian zoo official said on Wednesday.

"Our mahouts know the commands for elephants that are not known to their mahouts there. Sometimes mahouts are killed by elephants there, which is why many zoos are afraid of keeping male elephants," Central Zoo Authority member-secretary S.C. Sharma told Reuters.
"Once they learn this, they can have male as well as female elephants that can contribute towards better breeding of the species," he said.
The mahouts would be paid airfare and an allowance of about 500 stg ($800) a month, Sharma said. India gave two elephants to Britain earlier this year.
"But I doubt the proposal will take off. Most probably the governments of states with elephants will decide they cannot spare their mahouts for a month or more," he said. (1 stg=$1.6)
